items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1967-02-09
items.q: Then Buddy Petite's Band. When Jimmy Noon left to go to Chicago, I played with Buddy Petite and several other bands around New Orleans.

ctx.x: Can you tell us something about your training and taking lessons and so on?

Well, I started taking lessons around 9 years of age with my uncle, Wooden Joe Nicholas. He was my big influence on this jazz scene. And later on, I went to Papa Teo and took lessons with him for about a couple of years. Then Lorenzo Teo, his son. And finished up with him until around 1915. Then I started to go pro. My first gigs around New Orleans was with the Maple Leaf Band. Then Buddy Petite's Band. items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1972-06-26
items.q: Buddy Petit had a little band here.

ctx.x: That's the first thing you learn when you play music, all that noise. Mm-hmm.

To play music, you've got a phrase. Mm-hmm. You know, bring your notes up and down. You know, make it music-wise. I noticed that with these jazz bands around here. They still go loud, but maybe because they call them the public, you know, the poems like Danny Ball. You know, they don't get down and phrase, you know. Like Orenham used to do in the old days.
